title: Detection of digestive enzymes in the gut of Atlantic Salmon
projectDescription: The project aimed at determining the enzymatic machinery deployed by Salmo salar during digestion of two feeds that differed in their protein source.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Samples were obtained from two groups of salmon fed two different commercial diets (feed A and feed B). The two diets differed only in their protein source, whereas Feed A contained mostly plant-based proteins and feed B included mostly fish-based proteins. The salmon were fed one last time before they were taken out 40, 85 and 180 minutes after onset of feeding. Fish were euthanized, dissected, and the GIT carefully excised and opened to collect digesta contents from the stomach (ST), pyloric caeca (PC), midgut (MG), and hindgut (HG) Proteins in fish digesta were precipitated overnight using 12.5% ice-cold TCA. Proteins were processed following the S-Trap 96-well plate digestion protocol (PROTIFI, Farmingdale, NY, USA). Digestion was performed with 1.6 ng/µL trypsin (Promega, Madison, USA) for 1 h at 37 °C. Peptides were analyzed on a nanoLC-MS/MS system (Bruker) using DDA PASEF mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS raw files were processed using the FragPipe v21.1 for protein identification and label-free quantification (LFQ). MS and MS/MS spectra were searched against the a database consisting of the predicted salmon proteome, Ssal_v3.1 (NCBI RefSeq assembly GCF_905237065.1) and an in-house protein database built using the protein sequences derived from salmon microbial genome atlas. The final database (834,620 protein sequences) included with common contaminants (e.g., keratins, trypsin, and bovine serum albumin, 118 sequences). To estimate false discovery rates (FDRs), a decoy database consisting of reversed sequences of all protein entries was included. Trypsin was specified as the proteolytic enzyme, allowing one missed cleavage. Variable modifications included N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, deamidation of asparagine and glutamine residues, and pyro-glutamate formation at N-terminal glutamines, while carbamidomethylation of cysteines was set as a fixed modification
